title: Trump announces Budapest summit with Putin as Zelensky seeks Tomahawk missiles in Washington
body:
On 16 October 2025, US President Donald Trump held a telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump called it "very productive" and cited "great progress." Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said the call lasted almost two and a half hours and was the eighth between the two leaders that year. Trump announced that he would meet Putin in Budapest, Hungary, in the coming weeks, and that delegations from both countries would meet first, the following week. Ushakov said preparations would begin immediately.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Washington on the evening of 16 October and was due to meet Trump at the White House on 17 October. Zelensky was seeking long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles, and Trump remained noncommittal. According to the report, Putin warned that US supply of the missiles would not change the battlefield situation but would cause "significant damage" to relations between Russia and the United States. Zelensky said Russia was eager to resume dialogue once it heard about the Tomahawks.

Putin said Russia wanted a peaceful diplomatic settlement. Ushakov claimed that Russian forces held "complete strategic initiative" along the front and accused Ukraine of "terrorist methods" against civilian and energy targets.

The report covered events of 16 and 17 October and did not describe the outcome of the White House meeting. The planned Budapest summit was later cancelled.
